MAIN MESSAGE: This is a strategic partnership proposal, not a company introduction.

SCRIPT: "Good morning, and thank you for receiving us at TBEA headquarters. We have travelled here with one purpose. We believe Ulusoy and TBEA can build a long-term business together in Türkiye, the Balkans and the Middle East. Today we want to show you why we believe this, and to agree on the first practical steps."

TRANSITION: "Here is how we will take you through this today."

MAIN MESSAGE: The founding principle, "Everything on Time", applies directly to tenders and deliveries.

SCRIPT: "In the 1920s, our region on the Black Sea had no roads. When the river flooded, two towns were cut off. Our founder solved this first with a raft, then with trade, and in 1937 with the first Ulusoy coach. He gave the business one principle: Everything on Time. In your business, a late transformer can delay a whole power plant. Reliability and schedule discipline are exactly what we bring to tenders, deliveries and project coordination."

EMPHASISE: The link from "Everything on Time" to delivery discipline.

TRANSITION: "Three generations then built on this principle."

SLIDE 18 — Section 02: Why Türkiye matters now

SCRIPT: "Türkiye is entering a structural electricity and grid investment cycle. This is a long cycle, not a short boom. Let me show you five numbers."

SLIDE 19 — Demand is at record levels — and set to almost double by 2040

MAIN MESSAGE: Türkiye's electricity demand hit a record in 2025 and the official target is 680 TWh by 2040.

SCRIPT: "Türkiye consumed a record 361 terawatt-hours in 2025, with a record peak of almost 60 gigawatts. On 5 November, a few days ago, the Energy Minister presented the new national strategy for 2040. Demand is planned to rise to 680 terawatt-hours, almost double today. Installed capacity is planned to rise from 123 to 281 gigawatts. Behind every one of these gigawatts is a transformer, a switchgear bay and a cable."

EMPHASISE: "Five November, a few days ago": the information is fresh.

TRANSITION: "Where will this new capacity come from?"

LIKELY QUESTION: "Are these targets realistic? Turkish plans are often optimistic."
RESPONSE: "That is a fair challenge. Even the current-policies scenario in the same strategy reaches about 550 TWh by 2040, which is still a 50% increase. And the grid investment we show next is needed even at the lower scenario. We do not build our case on the highest number."
20:
SLIDE 20 — 127 GW installed — and wind + solar must almost triple by 2035

MAIN MESSAGE: Wind and solar must grow from about 44 GW to 120 GW by 2035, which means 8–10 GW a year.

SCRIPT: "Türkiye has 127 gigawatts installed today. Solar is now 28 gigawatts, more than natural gas. The official target is 120 gigawatts of wind and solar by 2035, against about 44 today. To reach it, Türkiye must add 8 to 10 gigawatts every year. The record so far is about 6.5. So the pace must increase, and every additional gigawatt needs step-up transformers, switchgear, cables and a grid connection."

TRANSITION: "Generation alone is not enough. The grid must grow too."

LIKELY QUESTION: "Who supplies the inverters and transformers for these plants today?"
RESPONSE: "A mix of Turkish manufacturers, European groups and Chinese suppliers. Inverters are already heavily Chinese. Transformers and high-voltage switchgear are more contested, and local factories are full. We will come back to this on the competition slide."

SCRIPT: "The government plans 28 billion dollars of transmission investment by 2035. That includes 15,000 kilometres of new AC lines and about 9,600 kilometres of HVDC corridors. SCRIPT: "In 2022 and 2023 Türkiye gave licences for wind and solar plants with integrated storage. The rule is that storage capacity must equal the plant's capacity. About 33 gigawatts of these licences exist, more than in any EU country. But in early 2026 only about 0.2 gigawatts was installed. The government expects 2 to 3 gigawatts to come online from 2026, and the target is 140 gigawatt-hours by 2040. New regulations this year also allow storage in industrial zones and at consumer sites."

EMPHASISE: The gap between 33 GW licensed and 0.2 GW installed.

TRANSITION: "Two more new sources of demand are data centers and industry."

LIKELY QUESTION: "Will all 33 GW really be built?"
RESPONSE: "No, certainly not all of it. Many licences will be delayed or cancelled. But even a fraction is several gigawatts of PCS, battery systems, MV skids and transformers. And it is a private market, where price, delivery and bankability matter more than domestic preference."

In the first half of 2026 it was applied in about 40% of tenders open to foreign bidders. It does not apply to private procurement, and in World Bank-financed contracts it applies only if the bidding documents say so."

SLIDE 28 — Private 154 kV connection substations for renewables and storage

MAIN MESSAGE: Every new renewable or hybrid plant needs a connection substation. These are usually procured privately, and that is TBEA's best first door.

SCRIPT: "Every wind, solar or hybrid-storage plant in Türkiye collects power at 33 kilovolts and connects to the TEİAŞ grid at 154 or 400 kilovolts. TRANSITION: "The second priority route is internationally financed."

LIKELY QUESTION: "Is TBEA equipment already accepted by TEİAŞ?"
